source_text.body:
Produce newsletter articles with images and Substack drafts
Claude Cowork interviews the newsletter owner, drafts five articles, makes featured images with Midjourney, and sets up drafts in Substack, now run as a batch SOP.
·
Feb 11, 2026
Done with
CW
Claude Cowork
What they did
One newsletter owner used Claude Cowork for an end-to-end content workflow. It first ran a 100-question voice interview to learn their material, voice, formatting preferences, and audience, then drafted five articles, used their Midjourney account for featured images, and logged into their Substack to create drafts, apply settings, check formatting, and attach images; the owner initially watched closely and had to log into each system first.
How it went
They turned the process into a reusable SOP for new Cowork task chats. The batch workflow replaced work that had taken about four hours per article, though the user said Canva image editing was clunky and they still do the final review and scheduling.
Worth knowing
The key catch was the first run: they had to pre-log into the tools and supervise closely to see what Cowork could and couldn’t handle.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Cowork
Copy prompt
I run a newsletter about [topic] for [audience]. Interview me with about [5] questions to pull out my ideas, then draft [5] articles in my voice and suggest a featured image idea for each. When finished, give me the drafts in a folder as separate documents with image prompts, and pause and show me before publishing or posting anything to [Substack or platform].
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeCowork/comments/1r2134o/what_are_your_use_cases_for_cowork
